prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (2001)

Family, education, universities
- Tax changes: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under-5s; new transferable tax allowance within marriage where there are children under 11 or a carer; remove tax on Widowed Mother’s/Parent’s Allowance; reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid to the caring parent; “Family Scholarships” for parents returning to work.
- Schools: expand autonomy via “Free Schools” run by heads/governors; allow popular schools to expand and new schools to open (including faith, parent and charitable providers); simpler exclusions with off-site Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; parents can trigger Ofsted inspections with management change if failing; streamline funding to reach schools directly per pupil.
- Students and universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000 income; no top-up fees; create permanent endowment funds to secure university independence.

Policing, crime, justice
- Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (e.g., paperwork done on the beat); enable parish constables; focus on antisocial behaviour.
- Young offenders: expand Secure Training Centre places with conditional release.
- Drugs: tougher action on dealers, mandatory prison for selling to under-16s; aggravated sentencing near schools.
- Sentencing: end automatic early release; sentences served as handed down; require prisoners to work, contributing to victim reparation/family support.
- Stronger supervision of sex offenders; new online child-protection laws.
- Victims: named contacts in police/CPS; reasons required for dropped/reduced charges; review self-defence and double jeopardy rules.

Economy, tax, regulation
- Targeted tax cuts totalling £8bn funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence, including: abolish tax on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; new Married Couple’s Allowance; 6p/litre cut in fuel duty; reduce business rates; repeal IR35; reliefs for regeneration and approved share options.
- Transparency: taxpayer statements; National Accounts Commission; simpler Capital Gains Tax.
- Deregulation: regulatory budgets cut annually; small-business exemptions; refocus utility regulators on competition; abolish Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear.
- Macroeconomy: keep the pound; enhance central bank independence; external fiscal oversight.

Health and care
- Match planned NHS funding but end political micro-management.
- Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits by clinical need (starting with cancer/cardiac); right to treatment elsewhere (NHS/private) if exceeded.
- GP/patient choice of hospital; expand nurse roles; standalone surgical units for high-volume procedures; Exceptional Medicines Fund; restore ward-level authority (Matron/Ward Sisters).
- Remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable; increase hospice funding; allow proven complementary therapies.

Pensions and ageing
- Raise basic pension (larger uplift for over-75s); option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence/bonus into a higher tax-free pension; increase age allowance by £2,000; abolish most taxes on savings; end compulsory annuitisation at 75; explore funded alternatives for younger workers; protect assets for long-term care; free nursing care.

Foreign, defence, trade, asylum
- EU: keep the pound; retain vetoes; seek flexibility clauses; stronger competition and anti-fraud; amend domestic law with reserved powers.
- Defence: meet manning needs; align commitments/capabilities; reserves reform; support European defence only within NATO; back ballistic missile defence; maintain independent deterrent.
- Development: work toward 0.7% GNP; more via charities; tighten multilateral aid performance; focus on governance and anti-corruption; appoint Envoy for Religious Freedom.
- Trade: pursue EU–NAFTA free trade area toward global free trade by 2020; merge diplomacy and trade functions.
- Asylum: secure reception centres until decisions; safe-country presumption; new Removals Agency for swift deportations.

Society, welfare, disability
- Office of Civil Society; abolish irrecoverable VAT for charities (funded by reallocations).
- Replace New Deal with outcome-paid “Britain Works” focused on sustained jobs; “Can Work, Must Work” principle; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
- Disability: higher savings disregard; new agency to pair Incapacity Benefit with rehab aids; national anti-fraud squad; clean National Insurance records.

Town, country, transport, environment, culture, media
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; renegotiate CAP/CFP; honesty in food labelling; rural rate cuts; benefit card to sustain post offices; local control of housing targets; protect waterways (“Blue Belts”); Rural Affairs select committee.
- Urban regeneration: local Regeneration Companies; extra policing, partner schools, estate renewal; tougher action on nuisance and antisocial tenants; ease brownfield development; expand Right to Buy; rent-to-mortgage; homesteading empty homes.
- Transport: cut fuel duty 6p/litre; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph on safe motorways; charge foreign lorries; revitalise rail; implement Cullen; support London Underground reform.
- Environment: meet climate goals via trading, efficiency, renewables, cleaner generation.
- Culture and sport: privatise Channel 4; £3bn cultural endowment (lottery surpluses included); simpler lottery access; boost tourism bodies; protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; streamline sports governance.
- Media: single converged regulator; liberalise ownership with protections; independent BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

Constitution and governance
- Devolve power to high-performing “free councils”; local referendums for large tax rises; abolish regional agencies/assemblies; restore enterprise functions to counties.
- Only relevant MPs to vote on England/Wales-only laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and a substantial elected element; stronger select committee independence; PM to face the Commons more frequently; retain current general election voting system.
- Reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and special advisers.
